lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic building a shortlist that survives scrutiny task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Using the research and reflections from the whole unit, the learner assembles a single shortlist document comparing at least two pathways side by side on requirements, deadlines, cost and funding categories, and setting/support fit, then walks a guardian through the shortlist so the guardian can ask questions and flag anything that looks incomplete or unrealistic before it is finalized.
safetyNotes: The guardian review is a conversation with the learner's own guardian about the shortlist document; no outside person is contacted for this lesson.
The shortlist may reference general cost and funding categories from day 3 but does not require any real household financial figures to be added or reviewed.

simulationAlternative.description: If a guardian review cannot happen this session, the learner instead completes the shortlist independently and has a trusted adult at their learning site review it using the same guiding questions, with a guardian confirming afterward that the finished shortlist was seen.

materials: learner-local: the learner's day 1-4 notes and research from this unit
adult-or-local: a guardian to review the shortlist with

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is the single most useful thing you learned across this unit that changed how you're thinking about your postsecondary options, and why did it matter?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Shortlist completeness: Shortlist includes all four required elements for both pathways, pulled from the unit's earlier research. | Genuine comparison, not parallel lists: The shortlist directly compares the two pathways on at least two of the four elements. | Guardian scrutiny incorporated: A specific guardian question or concern is named along with the learner's response to it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a third pathway from their day-1 list to the shortlist as a backup option, including at minimum its closest deadline and one requirement, so the shortlist has a fallback if either primary pathway falls through.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic building a shortlist that survives scrutiny task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using the research and reflections from the whole unit, the learner assembles a single shortlist document comparing at least two pathways side by side on requirements, deadlines, cost and funding categories, and setting/support fit, then walks a guardian through the shortlist so the guardian can ask questions and flag anything that looks incomplete or unrealistic before it is finalized.

Model move 2: Before assembling the shortlist, choose the two pathways you will compare and state why they are the right two to put side by side.
Model move 3: Build the side-by-side shortlist, pulling in requirements, timelines, cost and funding categories, and fit notes from earlier in the unit.

Model check: Shortlist completeness: Shortlist includes all four required elements for both pathways, pulled from the unit's earlier research. | Genuine comparison, not parallel lists: The shortlist directly compares the two pathways on at least two of the four elements. | Guardian scrutiny incorporated: A specific guardian question or concern is named along with the learner's response to it.

resources.title: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for building a shortlist that survives scrutiny.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using the research and reflections from the whole unit, the learner assembles a single shortlist document comparing at least two pathways side by side on requirements, deadlines, cost and funding categories, and setting/support fit, then walks a guardian through the shortlist so the guardian can ask questions and flag anything that looks incomplete or unrealistic before it is finalized.
Coach direction: Before assembling the shortlist, choose the two pathways you will compare and state why they are the right two to put side by side.
Learner prompt: Which two pathways will you compare on your shortlist, and why are these two the most useful comparison right now, rather than any other pair?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Build the side-by-side shortlist, pulling in requirements, timelines, cost and funding categories, and fit notes from earlier in the unit.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My shortlist includes, for both pathways, the actual entry requirements and a realistic timeline from day 2.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My shortlist includes, for both pathways, the general cost and funding categories from day 3.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My shortlist includes, for both pathways, the setting and support fit notes from day 4.
Response 4 (t2-p4): State the single closest deadline across both pathways, and what needs to happen before that deadline.

Equal-access rule: If a guardian review cannot happen this session, the learner instead completes the shortlist independently and has a trusted adult at their learning site review it using the same guiding questions, with a guardian confirming afterward that the finished shortlist was seen.

resources.title: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is the single most useful thing you learned across this unit that changed how you're thinking about your postsecondary options, and why did it matter?

Success checks: Shortlist completeness: Shortlist includes all four required elements for both pathways, pulled from the unit's earlier research. | Genuine comparison, not parallel lists: The shortlist directly compares the two pathways on at least two of the four elements. | Guardian scrutiny incorporated: A specific guardian question or concern is named along with the learner's response to it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: building a shortlist that survives scrutiny supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional building a shortlist that survives scrutiny condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Shortlist completeness: Shortlist includes all four required elements for both pathways, pulled from the unit's earlier research. | Genuine comparison, not parallel lists: The shortlist directly compares the two pathways on at least two of the four elements. | Guardian scrutiny incorporated: A specific guardian question or concern is named along with the learner's response to it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u01-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
